title: Hempstead Lake State Park: Native Heritage Learning
summary: The Montaukett Indian Nation’s November 2022 newsletter invited the public to a Native American Heritage Month program at Hempstead Lake State Park.

why_this_matters: The Montaukett Nation’s 2022 invitation places Native cultural education in a familiar Nassau County park. Together with the park’s environmental programs, it offers a way to learn about continuing Native presence and the care of shared waterways.
introduction_title: An Invitation from the Montaukett Nation
introduction_content: In its November 1, 2022 newsletter, signed by Chief Robert Pharaoh, the Montaukett Indian Nation invited members, family, and friends to public educational experiences celebrating Native culture and heritage. Hempstead Lake State Park was listed for November 5.1
history_content:
The Montaukett Nation’s invitation welcomed people to learn about Native culture and heritage at Hempstead Lake State Park. It was part of the Nation’s public outreach during Native American Heritage Month in 2022.1

Today the park’s Environmental Education and Resiliency Center offers programs about the surrounding landscape. See the park calendar for upcoming events.2

2021: a new place for environmental learning

New York State announced the opening of the park’s Environmental Education and Resiliency Center on September 23, 2021. Its hands-on exhibits explore storms, environmental management and the Mill River watershed. The center also provides space for community education.3

Native people as teachers of their own history

The Montaukett Nation’s invitation matters because the Nation speaks directly to members, families, and the wider public. Its 2022 Heritage Month outreach places contemporary Native culture within a public park, extending a history often encountered locally through colonial documents or roadside signs.1

Hempstead Lake belongs to the Mill River watershed. Downstream, the Lister Park panel introduces fishing, seasonal movement, and colonial displacement. Reading the two places together connects a historical interpretation of the river with a living nation’s invitation to learn. The Environmental Education and Resiliency Center adds a setting for understanding the watershed’s environmental changes.24
whereintheworld_content:
The pin marks the Environmental Education and Resiliency Center at Field 1, 880 Lake Drive, West Hempstead, a starting point for learning about the park today.5

Check New York State Parks for current programs, entrances and fees.2
